items.subject: FUJI_RESET
items.text: No reply at all: the base handler table runs first (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Fuji.cpp:215) and never ACKs; rs232Fuji's case FUJI_RESET -> fujicmd_reset(), which would ACK first (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:405-411), is unreachable

items.subject: FUJI_DEVICE_READY
items.text: Debug/test command left in the RS232 switch; one of only two commands reached through rs232Fuji's own switch.

items.subject: FUJI_STATUS
items.text: Always 4 zero bytes. rs232_status() (reqtype 1 = per-drive mount times, 8 x time_t) is dead code: base table handles FUJI_STATUS before the rs232 switch . The switch's paramCount<1 NAK is also unreachable.

items.subject: FUJI_GET_ADAPTERCONFIG
items.text: fn_version is truncated to 14 characters

items.subject: FUJI_GET_ADAPTERCONFIG_EXTENDED
items.text: String fields are filled even when not connected

items.subject: FUJI_SCAN_NETWORKS
items.text: ESP32 scan is blocking and temporarily disconnects an associated station

items.subject: FUJI_SET_SSID
items.text: Failure sends two NAK frames: fujicore_net_set_ssid_success() NAKs  and fujicmd_net_set_ssid_success() NAKs again (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:569). fujinet-lib resyncs on the next SLIP_END (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/port_slip.c:56-68) and so reads the stray NAK as the reply to the NEXT command: replies run one behind.

items.subject: FUJI_SET_SSID
items.text: ACK does not mean associated: ESP32 connect() returns esp_wifi_connect()'s immediate status ; a wrong password is ACKed and saved.

items.subject: FUJI_GET_SSID
items.text: Returns the saved WiFi passphrase in plain text

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_HOST_SLOTS
items.text: Buffer is not zeroed : a payload shorter than 256 bytes fills the remaining slots with stack garbage.

items.subject: FUJI_MOUNT_HOST
items.text: Once hostMounted is set the mount is not retried  even if the server went away.

items.subject: FUJI_UNMOUNT_HOST
items.text: On the SD host the disks are unmounted and their slots cleared BEFORE the NAK

items.subject: FUJI_UNMOUNT_HOST
items.text: MOUNT_ALL and COPY_FILE mount hosts without setting hostMounted, so UNMOUNT_HOST after them NAKs.

items.subject: FUJI_SET_HOST_PREFIX
items.text: COPY_FILE breaks once a prefix longer than "/" is set (see FUJI_COPY_FILE).

items.subject: FUJI_GET_HOST_PREFIX
items.text: prefix[] is never zeroed ; strlcpy writes only up to the NUL (fn-h89/lib/fuji/fujiHost.cpp:300-306): the tail of the reply is garbage.

items.subject: FUJI_OPEN_DIRECTORY
items.text: MOUNT_HOST first: dir_open fails on an unmounted host.

items.subject: FUJI_OPEN_DIRECTORY
items.text: With a path < 253 chars the pattern pointer is never null; an empty pattern is passed as ""

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DIR_ENTRY
items.text: addtl 0xC0 (block mode, group size 0) divides by zero at fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:887 -> SIGFPE on fujinet-pc, panic/reboot on ESP32.

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DIR_ENTRY
items.text: With 0x80 keep maxlen >= 14: set_additional_direntry_details does uint8_t maxlen -= 12 , smaller values wrap and the reply is cut mid-header.

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DIR_ENTRY
items.text: TRUNC flag and slash rules disagree by one for directories: a dir name of maxlen-13 chars gets TRUNC although only the '/' was dropped; one of maxlen-14 chars gets neither '/' nor TRUNC

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DIR_ENTRY
items.text: Plain .img files report mediatype 0 (unknown), not 1

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: Empty slots report mode 0x01 .

items.subject: FUJI_READ_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: mode reflects SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH / WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS, not the mode passed to MOUNT_IMAGE .

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: Filenames in the payload are ignored: fujiDisk::reset(fname, ...) never copies fname . Paths can only be set with SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH.

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: hostSlot 0xFF drops the slot from fnconfig.ini (path gone after restart) while the RAM filename stays and READ_DEVICE_SLOTS still shows it

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: No host-slot validation: a value 8..254 with an existing filename makes MOUNT_ALL use _fnHosts[] out of bounds

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS
items.text: Buffer not zeroed : a short payload gives the remaining slots garbage host/mode.

items.subject: FUJI_SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH
items.text: Missing field aborts the firmware: the rs232 switch's paramCount<3 guard  is unreachable.

items.subject: FUJI_MOUNT_IMAGE
items.text: ROM-type extensions  push the whole file before replying: FujiNet sends its own command frames to device 0xFF (NET_OPEN 0x4F with 5-byte payload id+u32 size, NET_WRITE 0x57 chunks, NET_CLOSE 0x43 [+0x01 abort]) and waits for ACKs (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/disk.cpp:28-110, 305-315; fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.h:178-186). On the H89 a .BIN file is therefore not a disk image.

items.subject: FUJI_MOUNT_IMAGE
items.text: Needs filename+host from SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH (or saved config) and a mounted host; it does not mount the host itself.

items.subject: FUJI_MOUNT_IMAGE
items.text: Repeated MOUNT_IMAGE with a prefix set re-applies the prefix to the already-prefixed filename.

items.subject: FUJI_MOUNT_ALL
items.text: Out-of-range host_slot 8..254 (possible via WRITE_DEVICE_SLOTS) indexes _fnHosts out of bounds

items.subject: FUJI_NEW_DISK
items.text: Leaves a 0-byte file behind and a dangling _fnDisks[slot].fileh (closed handle never set to nullptr, fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Fuji.cpp:150,159); fileh != nullptr is what image rotation tests

items.subject: FUJI_NEW_DISK
items.text: Reached only through rs232Fuji's switch (not in the base table).

items.subject: FUJI_SET_BOOT_MODE
items.text: Mode 0 puts the RS232 MS-DOS boot disk (360 KB FAT12, fn-h89/data/webui/device_specific/BUILD_RS232/autorun.img) on drive 0x31 even though setup() deliberately skips it on PINMAP_H89

items.subject: FUJI_SET_BOOT_MODE
items.text: Always ACKs: invalid mode, missing image (only autorun.img ships for BUILD_RS232) or TNFS failure mount nothing silently

items.subject: FUJI_CONFIG_BOOT
items.text: Despite the name it never changes boot_config or the saved config; boot_config is only written, never read, on BUILD_RS232.

items.subject: FUJI_COPY_FILE
items.text: Fails whenever a host prefix longer than "/" is set: each path is opened with fullpathlen = path length + 1 (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:1126-1132), so prefix+path never fits and fnfile_open returns null

items.subject: FUJI_COPY_FILE
items.text: The trailing-'/' rule only works if the LAST payload byte is '/': a NUL-terminated or padded spec disables it.

items.subject: FUJI_COPY_FILE
items.text: fread/fwrite results are not checked: a short copy still ACKs

items.subject: FUJI_COPY_FILE
items.text: Missing field aborts: the rs232 switch's guard  is unreachable.

items.subject: FUJI_OPEN_APPKEY
items.text: Any mode other than 0xFF is accepted; mode 2 still reads only 64 bytes .

items.subject: FUJI_READ_APPKEY
items.text: Never NAKs: no SD, no OPEN, OPEN in write mode, or missing file all return ACK with length 0

items.subject: FUJI_WRITE_APPKEY
items.text: An empty/missing payload writes a 0-byte key (truncating an existing one) and ACKs

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_ENCODE_INPUT
items.text: transaction_get's result is ignored : no payload appends len zero bytes and ACKs.

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_ENCODE_INPUT
items.text: Encode and decode share ONE buffer  and there is no clear command: unread output from a previous operation is prepended to the next input.

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_ENCODE_COMPUTE
items.text: Output uses the standard alphabet with '=' padding AND inserts '\n' after every 72 characters plus a final '\n' ; ENCODE_LENGTH counts them.

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_DECODE_INPUT
items.text: Payload result ignored : missing payload appends zeros and ACKs.

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_DECODE_INPUT
items.text: Encode and decode share ONE buffer  and there is no clear command: unread output from a previous operation is prepended to the next input.

items.subject: FUJI_BASE64_DECODE_COMPUTE
items.text: Encode and decode share ONE buffer  and there is no clear command: unread output from a previous operation is prepended to the next input.

items.subject: FUJI_HASH_INPUT
items.text: Payload result ignored : missing payload hashes len zero bytes.

items.subject: FUJI_HASH_COMPUTE
items.text: Unknown algorithm still ACKs, leaves an empty digest (LENGTH 0, OUTPUT 0 bytes) and still clears the data.

items.subject: FUJI_HASH_LENGTH
items.text: Reply is ONE byte, unlike the u32 Base64/QR lengths.

items.subject: FUJI_QRCODE_INPUT
items.text: Payload result ignored

items.subject: FUJI_QRCODE_ENCODE
items.text: All three fields are required: a two-field packet aborts the firmware.

items.subject: FUJI_QRCODE_LENGTH
items.text: After OUTPUT has consumed the whole code, LENGTH returns 0 and cannot re-render.

items.subject: FUJI_SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH (emptying a slot)
items.text: An empty path sets the slot's host slot to FFH but leaves the old path, which FUJI_GET_DEVICE_FULLPATH still returns: the slot is not emptied. And a request that itself gives host slot FFH (what FUJI_READ_DEVICE_SLOTS reports for an empty slot) is refused with NAK, even with an empty path. Only FUJI_UNMOUNT_IMAGE empties a slot.

items.subject: FUJI_COPY_FILE (time)
items.text: The ACK comes only when the copy is finished. A 161,280-byte image from tnfs.fujinet.online took from 14.4 to 18.2 s in six runs, four of them more than the 15 s that fujinet-lib and the book's library wait for a reply (see L21).

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: Two fields are mandatory even when aux2 is 0; one field (or a single u16) crashes the firmware

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: On TNFS:// and SD:// an aux1 other than 4/6/7/8/9/12 reaches abort() - firmware reboot

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: A '*' in a non-directory URL (e.g. in an HTTP query string) is turned into NUL and truncates the URL

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: A URL ending in '.' loses the dot

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: Terminate the spec with NUL or CR LF; a lone CR stays inside the URL

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: HTTP aux1 4 and 8 URL-encode the path (so do not pre-encode); 5/9/12/13/14 send it verbatim

items.subject: NET_OPEN
items.text: UDP OPEN without a port NAKs but leaves STATUS err = 1 (error never set)

items.subject: NET_CLOSE
items.text: HTTP POST (aux1 13/14) and DELETE (5/9) are never sent if no STATUS/READ happened before CLOSE: resultCode 0 means 'no transaction' and close just succeeds

items.subject: NET_READ
items.text: TCP: READ with nothing pre-buffered asks the socket for exactly 'length'; a short read NAKs with err 202 and the bytes that did arrive are thrown away . Always STATUS first (it pre-reads into the buffer, Protocol.cpp:169-175) and ask for no more than bytes-waiting

items.subject: NET_READ
items.text: HTTP body with nothing buffered: client read short -> NAK and the partial bytes are lost

items.subject: NET_READ
items.text: UDP with empty buffer pads the reply with zero bytes up to 'length'

items.subject: NET_READ
items.text: HTTP GET_HEADERS mode: each READ consumes one header and copies exactly 'length' bytes from it (over-read when length > header); a READ after the last header indexes past the vector - undefined, may crash

items.subject: NET_READ
items.text: If NET_SET_PARSER was sent while no channel was open, READ dereferences a null protocol - crash

items.subject: NET_WRITE
items.text: Payload shorter than the length field: zero bytes are appended up to 'length' and written ; longer: the excess is ignored

items.subject: NET_WRITE
items.text: A failed write leaves its bytes in the transmit buffer; they are prepended to the next WRITE and retried at CLOSE (FS.cpp:351-356, TCP.cpp:166-196, Protocol.cpp:127-128). NET_SET_HTTP_MODE clears the buffer

items.subject: NET_WRITE
items.text: Write translation looks for the full native EOL (CR LF unless NET_SET_EOL changed it); a lone CR is not translated

items.subject: NET_WRITE
items.text: A STATUS on an HTTP PUT channel before CLOSE fires the PUT early with the data so far (empty body -> client returns -1 -> err 144); CLOSE then PUTs again

items.subject: NET_STATUS
items.text: No channel: 00 00 00 CF (207 NOT_CONNECTED) (NDevice.cpp:309-314); after a failed OPEN or CLOSE: 00 00 00 <reason>

items.subject: NET_STATUS
items.text: UDP under-reports: STATUS pre-reads the waiting datagram into the receive buffer, then computes avail from udp.available() - the NEXT datagram - so a single pending datagram shows avail 0 . The datagram is still returned by a READ

items.subject: NET_STATUS
items.text: err 136 appears as soon as an FS file or HTTP body is fully consumed, including right after a JSON PARSE (body consumed) and before QUERY fills the buffer

items.subject: NET_STATUS
items.text: After a failed PARSE err stays 213 (JSON) or 144 (HTML/XML) on every STATUS

items.subject: NET_STATUS
items.text: HTTP GET_HEADERS mode: STATUS (and the background interrupt poll via available()) fires the request if not done yet

items.subject: NET_PARSE
items.text: On a stream that stays connected (e.g. TCP) PARSE does not return until the peer disconnects (fnjson.cpp:364); the H89 library times out after 15 s of silence

items.subject: NET_QUERY
items.text: Querying a value that is, or contains, an empty array [] crashes the firmware: the array loop dereferences a null child . Any query whose result includes [] - including the empty query on a document containing [] - triggers it

items.subject: NET_QUERY
items.text: Flag 0x04 with a string holding '<' but no later '>' loops forever

items.subject: NET_QUERY
items.text: HTML/XML: the RS232 handler keeps a trailing NUL and any bytes after it in the selector string  - send exactly the selector bytes
items.cite: rs232Network.cpp:9; fnhtml.cpp:80-112 compares/parses the whole std::string

items.subject: NET_QUERY
items.text: NET_SET_PARSER while no channel was open, then QUERY -> null protocol dereference crash

items.subject: NET_SET_PARAMETER
items.text: NET_SET_PARSER builds a fresh parser and resets flags and line ending: send SET_PARAMETER after SET_PARSER

items.subject: NET_SET_PARAMETER
items.text: param 1 with parser NONE after SET_PARSER-before-OPEN dereferences a null protocol

items.subject: NET_SET_PARSER
items.text: Does not check for an open channel: with none it creates a parser bound to a null protocol, and a later READ, QUERY, SEEK/TELL (mode 0) or SET_PARAMETER 1 (mode 0) crashes the firmware

items.subject: NET_SET_PARSER
items.text: OPEN resets the parser to NONE : send SET_PARSER after OPEN

items.subject: NET_SET_PARSER
items.text: Write HTTP POST data before switching to JSON - writes NAK afterwards

items.subject: NET_TRANSLATION
items.text: OR semantics: override 1 with aux2 2 gives mode 3 (CR LF)

items.subject: NET_SET_EOL
items.text: A NUL terminator in the payload becomes part of the line ending

items.subject: NET_SET_INT_RATE
items.text: rate 0: poll_interrupt divides by timerRate*2 - integer division by zero, firmware crash once a channel is open on that unit (NDevice.cpp:861,867); poll_interrupt runs on the H89 card too

items.subject: NET_SET_INT_RATE
items.text: On the H89 card the data-ready signal goes nowhere: ESP32 calls setRI(), a no-op on PPIChannel (rs232.cpp:186-187, PPIChannel.h:48); fujinet-pc drives DTR/RTS only on a real serial port with serial_proceed configured, never under BoIP

items.subject: NET_SEEK
items.text: The seek is performed twice  - on HTTP that is two Range requests

items.subject: NET_TELL
items.text: No channel: the 4 bytes are uninitialised stack contents - u32le_t has no constructor

items.subject: NET_TELL
items.text: TNFS/SD: the seek(0,SEEK_CUR) clears the receive buffer, so bytes STATUS pre-read (translation read-ahead) are discarded and the position reported is past them

items.subject: NET_TELL
items.text: HTTP reports bytes fetched from the server so far

items.subject: NET_TELL
items.text: Parser NONE bound to a null protocol (SET_PARSER before OPEN) -> crash

items.subject: NET_CHDIR
items.text: CR/LF are NOT stripped (unlike OPEN): a CR LF-terminated payload puts CR LF into the prefix and into every later relative OPEN

items.subject: NET_CHDIR
items.text: A packet with no payload clears the prefix

items.subject: NET_USERNAME
items.text: If the user name is empty the password is not passed either

items.subject: NET_PASSWORD
items.text: Ignored unless a user name is also set

items.subject: NET_RENAME
items.text: Kills whatever channel was open on the unit - buffered writes/HTTP PUT lost, no close

items.subject: NET_RENAME
items.text: Failure reason is lost: STATUS afterwards says 207

items.subject: NET_RENAME
items.text: TNFS without a comma ACKs and does nothing

items.subject: NET_RENAME
items.text: FTP: ACK, nothing done (FTP.h:37); GDRIVE has no override - only parses, ACKs

items.subject: NET_RENAME
items.text: HTTP: WebDAV MOVE with Destination set to a server path, not a full URL

items.subject: NET_DELETE
items.text: FTP: ACK, nothing deleted

items.subject: NET_DELETE
items.text: channel on the unit destroyed; error reason lost

items.subject: NET_LOCK
items.text: Silent no-op ACK on FTP (FTP.h:65), NFS (NFS.cpp:360-363) and every protocol without an override - HTTP, SMB, S3, GDRIVE, ONEDRIVE

items.subject: NET_UNLOCK
items.text: Silent no-op ACK where not implemented
items.cite: FS.h:131; NFS.cpp:365-368; FTP has no unlock override so the FS default applies

items.subject: NET_MKDIR
items.text: FTP: ACK, nothing created

items.subject: NET_MKDIR
items.text: TNFS MKDIR/RMDIR never unmount their session

items.subject: NET_RMDIR
items.text: FTP: ACK, nothing removed

items.subject: NET_ACCEPT
items.text: Poll STATUS first: on a listener with no client 'connected' = 1 means a client is waiting

items.subject: NET_CLOSE_CLIENT
items.text: Return value inverted: NAK = client closed, ACK = nothing was closed

items.subject: NET_SET_HTTP_MODE
items.text: Any response bytes still buffered are discarded by the mode switch

items.subject: NET_GET_REMOTE
items.text: Overwrites the first ~22 bytes of an unread datagram, and writes past the string's allocation when the receive buffer is empty/small; then sends 256 bytes read from that storage

items.subject: NET_GET_REMOTE
items.text: Before any datagram arrived the address is fnUDP's initial remote_ip/remote_port

items.subject: NET_SET_DESTINATION
items.text: ESP32 extracts the host with substr(first_colon+1, last_colon-2), correct only when the first colon is at index 1: 'N:host:port' works, 'N1:host:port' yields 'host:' and sends fail

items.subject: NET_SET_DESTINATION
items.text: fujinet-pc builds the string with strlen on a payload that is not NUL-terminated - send a trailing NUL

items.subject: NET_SET_DESTINATION
items.text: Any STATUS after a datagram arrives replaces the destination with that datagram's sender

items.subject: NET_QUERY (ASCII flag)
items.text: With query flag 10H (ASCII output) a JSON string's LF line ending is turned into a space, which network_json_query() does not strip: "FujiNet " comes back for "FujiNet". Numbers are not affected.

items.subject: NET_READ on HTTP (correction)
items.text: A READ larger than what is buffered returns what is there (FS.cpp caps the request to available()); it NAKs only when nothing is available.

items.subject: NET_GET_REMOTE
items.text: Overwrites a buffered datagram (the next READ returned '127.'); before any datagram it answers 255.255.255.255:0.

items.subject: framing
items.text: On 0xC0 the bus collects bytes until a second 0xC0 has been read; that span is the frame . A frame must therefore be exactly C0 <body> C0: a doubled leading C0 (C0 C0 <body> C0) produces an empty 2-byte frame that is rejected silently, the body bytes are then read as raw modem data, and the trailing C0 opens a bogus frame (derived from rs232.cpp:99-116 + 337-359 and FujiBusPacket.cpp:150-151)

items.subject: framing
items.text: Frame rejected if: encoded span < 8 bytes or does not start and end with 0xC0 ; decoded < 6 bytes (157-158); header length != decoded length (164-165); checksum mismatch (170-176); descriptor chain or fields run past the end (193-194, 212-213)

items.subject: params
items.text: param(n) returns _params.at(n).value as uint32 regardless of the field's wire size ; devices never check the field width, so a u8, u16 or u32 field all work where a number is expected

items.subject: params
items.text: A missing field makes .at() throw std::out_of_range. ESP32 H89 build has C++ exceptions off (fn-h89/sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:422) so it aborts (reboot); fujinet-pc terminates on the uncaught exception. Guarded: disk R/P/W (disk.cpp:385-388), disk STATUS (395-396), clock alt flag (rs232Clock.h:14-17), printer STATUS (printer.cpp:241). Unguarded: modem SET_DUMP, LISTEN, BAUDRATELOCK (2 fields), AUTOANSWER, STATUS

items.subject: replies
items.text: Data is attached only when ack is true; a NAK never carries data, even when the handler supplied some

items.subject: replies
items.text: Exactly one reply per accepted frame except: bad frame (silence), printer disabled , modem disabled (silence, modem.cpp:1612-1615), modem ACK/NAK (no bytes), and ROM mount pushes (extra unsolicited frames to device 0xFF before the Fuji reply, disk.cpp:28-110)

items.subject: replies
items.text: transaction_success asserts the state is NO_GET/DID_GET ; assertions are enabled on the ESP32 H89 build (sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:414), so a success after an error aborts (see modem LISTEN 0)

items.subject: errors
items.text: Read timeout inside a frame (gap longer than the channel read timeout): frame is incomplete, parse fails, silence (rs232.cpp:355-359, 365). The bytes that arrive after the gap are then read as raw modem data until the next C0

items.subject: errors
items.text: The bus does not consult device_active / enable state before dispatch ; each device decides

items.subject: DISK_READ
items.text: Sector numbers are 0-based although diskTypeImg.cpp:16 says '1-based'

items.subject: DISK_READ
items.text: A trailing partial 512-byte block of an IMG is unreachable: sector count = size/512 truncated

items.subject: DISK_READ
items.text: An IMD sector with a data error or deleted mark is still returned with ACK; only DISK_STATUS shows it

items.subject: DISK_WRITE
items.text: verify flag (WRITE vs PUT) is ignored by every media type

items.subject: DISK_WRITE
items.text: IMD out-of-range sector: sector_size()=0 -> zero-length get succeeds -> write() NAKs

items.subject: DISK_PUT
items.text: Identical to DISK_WRITE; the only difference  is ignored downstream

items.subject: DISK_STATUS
items.text: Answers even with nothing mounted: 00 FF E0 00

items.subject: DISK_STATUS
items.text: IMG never reports double density: _disk_sector_size stays at its 128 default  because MediaTypeImg::mount never sets it (diskTypeImg.cpp:157-166, 111-112). Normal IMG reply: 00 FF E0 00

items.subject: DISK_STATUS
items.text: ROM media: 00 00 00 00

items.subject: DISK_STATUS
items.text: After unmount the stale media object still answers

items.subject: DISK_STATUS
items.text: Was mapped onto WRITE before 7ab84ae64 (commit message); fixed at HEAD

items.subject: DISK_FORMAT
items.text: FORMAT does not format: IMG just ACKs

items.subject: DISK_FORMAT
items.text: Reply length is _disk_sector_size = 128, not 512

items.subject: DISK_FORMAT
items.text: No device_active check: after unmount an IMG drive still ACKs

items.subject: DISK_FORMAT_MEDIUM
items.text: Alias of DISK_FORMAT

items.subject: DISK_PERCOM_READ
items.text: IMG: all zeros, derive_percom_block is empty  - unless a DISK_PERCOM_WRITE stored something

items.subject: DISK_PERCOM_READ
items.text: IMD: filled at mount: tracks=max cyl+1, step 1, spt=max, sides=heads-1, density, sector_size=largest sector, drive_present 0xFF

items.subject: DISK_PERCOM_READ
items.text: Layout from fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskType.h:62-75

items.subject: DISK_PERCOM_WRITE
items.text: ACKs even with no payload: transaction_get result is ignored

items.subject: APETIME_GETTIME
items.text: Year byte is tm_year-100, i.e. two-digit year from 2000

items.subject: APETIME_GETTZTIME
items.text: With no alternate TZ set it falls back to the system TZ

items.subject: APETIME_SETTZ_ALT2
items.text: Despite the name this is the SIMPLE time GETTER on RS232: the read table claims 0x54 before the write table

items.subject: APETIME_GET_SOS
items.text: NUL included because rs232Clock does not override string_needs_null()

items.subject: APETIME_SETTZ
items.text: ACK is sent BEFORE validation ; an invalid TZ (e.g. payload starting with NUL, or a control char) is silently ignored but still ACKed

items.subject: APETIME_SETTZ
items.text: Any printable string is stored; POSIX validity is not checked

items.subject: APETIME_SETTZ_ALT
items.text: ACK before validation, invalid TZ silently dropped

items.subject: APETIME_SETTZ_ALT
items.text: Persists across reboots (writes config)

items.subject: PRINTER_WRITE
items.text: Buffer overrun: memcpy(provideBuffer(), data, len) with no bound into uint8_t buffer[320] - payloads > 320 bytes overwrite the emulator object

items.subject: PRINTER_WRITE
items.text: Length truncated to 8 bits: process(uint8_t linelen, ...) gets len mod 256, so 256 bytes print nothing (still ACK) and 300 bytes print the first 44

items.subject: PRINTER_WRITE
items.text: Default type FILE_TRIM writes up to and including the first 0x9B (ATASCII EOL) and drops the rest of the record . setEOL('\r') does not affect the file printer

items.subject: PRINTER_WRITE
items.text: FILE_ASCII drops CR and LF (keeps only 32..122 except 96, after &0x7F) so lines run together on the H89

items.subject: PRINTER_WRITE
items.text: Printer disabled in config -> no reply at all (silence), not a NAK (printer.cpp:226-229); default enabled

items.subject: PRINTER_PUT
items.text: Alias of PRINTER_WRITE

items.subject: PRINTER_STATUS
items.text: Byte 1 is an uninitialized member
items.cite: printer.h:27; printer.cpp:96; object created with new at main.cpp:360

items.subject: output
items.text: fujinet-pc writes the printer's output to the file paper in its SD directory.

items.subject: MODEM_CONTROL
items.text: No reply bytes at all

items.subject: MODEM_CONFIGURE
items.text: Always 9600 regardless of the request

items.subject: MODEM_SET_DUMP
items.text: Missing field aborts the firmware

items.subject: MODEM_LISTEN
items.text: port 0: transaction_error() then transaction_success() -> assert(state) fails -> abort on the ESP32 (assertions on)

items.subject: MODEM_BAUDRATELOCK
items.text: Two fields required

items.subject: MODEM_STATUS
items.text: Reply is 2 raw bytes, NOT a SLIP frame

items.subject: MODEM_WRITE
items.text: cmdOutput is forced false for the whole command  and every at_cmd_println() returns early when it is false (modem.cpp:468, 484, 504, 525): OK/ERROR/help/IP/echo text is never sent for commands given this way

items.subject: MODEM_WRITE
items.text: Numeric results (ATV0) still emit CR LF but the digits go to an unsent _packetData buffer

items.subject: MODEM_WRITE
items.text: No payload -> returns without action

items.subject: MODEM_STREAM
items.text: fujinet-pc on a TTY: the HOST LINK baud changes to modemBaud (e.g. 9600 after MODEM_CONFIGURE) (rs232.cpp:323-335); PPI: setBaudrate is a no-op (PPIChannel.h:39); BoIP: skipped

items.subject: MODEM_STREAM
items.text: Raw 9-byte reply, not a frame

items.subject: ATDT / ATA
items.text: After ATDT the far end's first data reaches the H89 before CONNECT (about a second ahead); after ATA a bare CR LF comes first, then the caller's data, then CONNECT.

items.subject: bare AT commands
items.text: AT commands sent as bytes outside a frame are acted on about 500 ms after the last byte (the BoIP channel's read timeout on fujinet-pc).

items.subject: CPM_INIT
items.text: Not registered, and ATCPM dereferences the null CPM pointer

items.subject: descriptor flags on the wire
items.text: fuji_bus_call puts its FUJI_FIELD_DATA (08H) and FUJI_FIELD_REPLY (10H) flags in the packet's descriptor byte. The firmware ignores bits 3-6, so no harm, but the bytes differ from other FujiBus clients'.

items.subject: port_putc
items.text: No timeout: with the FujiNet not running, a C program hangs in its first call.

items.subject: FUJI_DIR_ENTRY_IS_DIR / _IS_TRUNC
items.text: Use is_dir/is_trunc, which the H89's FujiDirEntry does not have (it has flags): code using them does not compile. Test flags & 1 and flags & 2.

items.subject: fixed 256-byte payloads
items.text: fuji_open_directory, fuji_set_host_prefix, fuji_set_device_filename and fuji_copy_file always send 256 bytes from the caller's string, so whatever follows its NUL is sent too (and the firmware may read it as a pattern or part of a path). Clear a 256-byte buffer first.

items.subject: network_json_query
items.text: Always sends 256 bytes of query and reads the answer into the caller's buffer with no limit.

items.subject: network_bus_read
items.text: Returns the length asked for on any ACK, even when fewer bytes came.

items.subject: fuji_get_wifi_enabled
items.text: Ignores whether the call succeeded and returns the last value it got.

items.subject: clock_get_time
items.text: Writes a NUL one byte past the reply: the buffer must be one byte longer than the format's reply.

items.subject: network_udp_set_destination
items.text: Sends the devicespec without a NUL and with the unit prefix (N7:), which the firmware reads wrongly; the datagram does not arrive. Use fuji_bus_call with 'N:host:port' and a NUL.

items.subject: network_read_nb
items.text: Busy-loops forever while STATUS says nothing waiting and no error, e.g. on UDP (whose STATUS under-reports) or an idle server.

items.subject: fuji_get_time, fuji_enable_device, fuji_disable_device
items.text: Send commands the H89's FujiNet does not have: always false.

items.subject: unlinkable
items.text: fn_error, network_proceed, network_has_proceed, network_get_dstats, fuji_enable_udpstream, fuji_get_device_enabled_status and _fuji_status are declared but not built for the H89.

items.subject: fuji_get_host_slots / fuji_get_device_slots
items.text: The count must be 8: the reply is always all eight slots, and a smaller buffer makes the call fail.

items.subject: network_unit
items.text: No range check: "N0:" addresses the FujiNet device (70H), so a network command arrives there as some other command (NET_SET_PARAMETER, FBH, as SET_SSID); "N9:" goes to 79H, "N10:" to unit 1.

items.subject: network_unit_status
items.text: Returns 0 on success (the macro is !fuji_bus_call).

items.subject: fuji_open_directory_filter
items.text: With a NULL pattern (which the header allows) it reads address 0 and sends what it finds as the pattern; with an empty one it sends the caller's memory after the path.

items.subject: fuji_hash_data / fuji_hash_calculate
items.text: Hex output has no NUL: the buffer needs fuji_hash_size() + 1.

items.subject: network_json_strip_newlines
items.text: Writes buffer[buflen], one past the data.

items.subject: qrcode_create
items.text: Returns negative NETWORK_ERROR codes (-162, -215), not FN_ERR values.

items.subject: port_getbuf_slip_dual
items.text: Does not read the closing END of a reply that fills its buffer exactly, which includes every bare ACK and NAK; the next read starts with a stray C0H. Harmless for fujinet-lib's own calls (they resynchronise on END), but a program mixing in raw reads (the modem) must drop it first.

items.subject: reply timeout
items.text: fuji_bus_call() waits a fixed 15 s (TIMEOUT_SLOW) for a reply and has no way to drop a reply that arrives later. When FUJI_COPY_FILE took longer, fuji_copy_file() returned false and the late ACK was taken as the reply to the next request (a STATUS), after which every reply was one behind and the test program reported the FujiNet BROKEN. With TIMEOUT_SLOW at 60 s the copy test passed. Proposed: a longer timeout for slow commands, and a drain before each request.

items.subject: network: line ending
items.text: BASIC_LINE_ENDING is "\n" for the H89, but the FujiNet's line ending on this bus is CR LF. The echo test opens with OPEN_TRANS_LF, so its LF comes back as CR LF, and the test, reading only as many bytes as it sent, compares CR with LF and stops: only 5 of the network program's 82 tests run. Fix: give the H89 "\r\n", as __WATCOMC__ has; then all 82 pass under both systems.

items.subject: disk: directory entry offset
items.text: DIRENTRY_FILENAME_OFFSET is 13 for the H89, but on this bus a FUJI_READ_DIR_ENTRY header is 12 bytes (as for MS-DOS), so the name is compared from its second letter and the copied lobby.dsk is never found. Fixed (the H89 given 12, as MS-DOS has) and with TIMEOUT_SLOW raised (L21), the disk test passes under both systems.

items.subject: fujidev: restoring a slot
items.text: The test puts back an empty drive slot with FUJI_SET_DEVICE_FULLPATH, an empty path and the host slot FFH it read. The firmware refuses FFH, and even with 0 it leaves the test's name in the slot (F90), so the read-back fails and drive slot 0 is left named /test_filename. Fix: put back an empty slot with fuji_unmount_disk_image(). Fixed so, all 88 of the fujidev program's tests pass under both systems.

items.subject: load address
items.text: The HDOS target's default CRT_ORG_CODE is 4480H: the split-octal address 042.200 (2280H) read as the plain octal number 042200. Programs work but waste 8.6K. Proposed fix: CRT_ORG_CODE = $2280 with a REGISTER_SP that is not inside the program.

items.subject: command line
items.text: With startup=3 the start-up code pushes the entry SP, moves the stack (crt_init_sp, crt_init_atexit), then pops from the NEW stack, so the command line is split with a wrong length and argv[] is damaged. Proposed fix: replace the push/pop with ld hl,(__restore_sp_onexit+1). The book builds with CRT_ENABLE_COMMANDLINE=0 and hdos_args().

items.subject: hdos.def
items.text: The HDOS system values (S_SYSM, S_USRM, S_DATE ...) are given 2000H too high, e.g. S_SYSM $40D0 for 20D0H: the same split-octal misreading.

items.subject: unsigned long %
items.text: In ISS.C, t % 60UL (and % 60, (t / 60UL) % 60UL, (t / 3600UL) % 24UL) gave wrong results for t = 1760270400: the seconds came out 36, which is the remainder of t's low 16 bits. Division of the same long was right. The book subtracts whole days and works in 16 bits instead. Seen under HDOS with sccz80's default options; not narrowed down further.
items.cite: observed: build/runs/iss-c-hdos (before the fix); src/c/iss/iss.c print_stamp()

items.subject: -l with a dotted library name
items.text: zcc -lfujinet.h89-hdos does not find fujinet.h89-hdos.lib (the dot stops .lib being added); give the name in full: -lfujinet.h89-hdos.lib.

items.area: fujinet-pc (the book's stand-in for the card)
items.subject: directory details
items.text: READ_DIR_ENTRY with 80H returns blank details (size 0, 1969-12-31, in the host's time zone) for files below the top of the SD directory, and network directory listings show size 0: dir_open looks files up in the wrong place. The card is not affected.

items.area: fujinet-pc (the book's stand-in for the card)
items.subject: WiFi
items.text: A stand-in: always connected to 'Dummy Cafe'; a scan finds 'Dummy Cafe 0'-'15'; SET_SSID always succeeds.

items.area: fujinet-pc (the book's stand-in for the card)
items.subject: shutdown with a TCP channel open
items.text: fujinet-pc crashed (segmentation fault) while shutting down, in NetworkProtocolTCP's destructor, each time it was stopped with a TCP channel still open: a connection, after fujinet-lib's network test had stopped early, and a listening channel, after the corrected test had finished. Only at shutdown; the card never shuts down this way.
